apps/mvp/worker/github/Pulls.ts:65: Unchanged reads do not advance ordering timestamps, allowing an intervening older snapshot with different values to overwrite the latest observed state; upsertReview has the same issue at line 114.

notes.why: `replaceCommits` has no newer-than guard and no transaction, so a delayed Apply can overwrite a newer commit list, leaving `pulls.head_sha` and `pull_commits` disagreeing until the next pull_request event. Agree with Astra's flag.
risks: apps/mvp/worker/github/Pulls.ts:83: two Apply runs for the same PR (rapid `synchronize` deliveries, one delayed by retry) can project in fetch-reverse order; `upsertPull` keeps the newer row via `source_updated_at`/`fetched_at` but `replaceCommits` takes whatever arrives last. Reconcile walks only the issues stream, so the stale list persists until the next webhook for that PR. Guard with the read's `fetchedAt` (store it on `pull_commits` or only replace when `upsertPull` applied or the row's `fetched_at` ≤ this read's).

apps/mvp/worker/github/Pulls.ts:89: DELETE then per-row INSERT with no `withTransaction` on the Apply path (`readPull` → `projectPull`), so a shape reader sees an empty or partial list mid-replace and a failure between statements leaves it that way until the next event; two concurrent replaces race to a unique-violation on `(item_id, position)`.

apps/mvp/worker/github/Pulls.ts:65: an unchanged read does not advance `fetched_at`, so a later-fetched read that observed the same values leaves the row's guard at the older `fetched_at`; a delayed earlier read carrying a field GitHub changes without bumping `updated_at` (`mergeable_state`, `merged_by`) then overwrites the newer observation. Same shape at line 114 for reviews. Self-heals on the next read.
apps/mvp/worker/github/Pulls.ts:123: a `gone` pull tombstones only the `items` row; `pulls`, `pull_commits` and `reviews` rows stay and the pulls shape keeps serving them.
